Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions to the equation  $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{5}{8},$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$   are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}, $\,x≈$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{5}{8})=0.675\,131…≈0.6751
$$

Since $0.675\,1$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=0.6751.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=0.6751.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.6751.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/cc57a94c1f4f4fa53e35930c053b8f2e3f2be0fee0beb8d1584835a0f134b800.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -0.675\,1 \\  & ≈2.4665\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are 

$$
x≈0.7,\,x≈2.5.
$$
